title: Kubernetes Examples
description: Small Kubernetes examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: A cluster and its tools
examples.description: A cluster is a group of machines managed together. kubectl is a command-line tool that asks the Kubernetes API about that cluster.

examples.title: Check the current context
examples.description: A context chooses a cluster, user and sometimes namespace. Read it first so you know where a command would act.
examples.code:
kubectl config current-context
kubectl config get-contexts

examples.title: Pods hold containers
examples.description: A Pod is Kubernetes' smallest runnable unit. Containers in one Pod share some resources, such as the network address.
examples.code:
Pod: club-web
Container: web server
Pod network address: shared by containers in that Pod

examples.title: Deployments manage replicas
examples.description: A Deployment describes how many matching Pods should run and how their template looks. A replica is one copy.
examples.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: club-web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: club-web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: club-web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:stable

examples.title: Labels group resources
examples.description: A label is a key-value marker attached to a resource. Selectors find resources with matching labels.

examples.title: Inspect resources
examples.description: get lists resources. describe gives a detailed human-readable view with events that can explain problems.
examples.code:
kubectl get pods
kubectl describe deployment club-web

examples.title: Services give a stable route
examples.description: A Service gives a stable way to reach a selected group of Pods. This example is internal to the cluster.
examples.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: club-web
spec:
  selector:
    app: club-web
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 80
  type: ClusterIP

examples.title: ConfigMaps hold ordinary settings
examples.description: A ConfigMap stores non-secret configuration. An application may read selected values through environment variables or files.
examples.code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: club-settings
data:
  WELCOME_TEXT: "Hello, club"

examples.title: Resource requests and limits
examples.description: Requests help schedule a container. Limits bound some resource use. CPU m means one thousandth of a CPU unit.
examples.code:
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "100m"
    memory: "64Mi"
  limits:
    cpu: "200m"
    memory: "128Mi"

examples.title: Readiness and liveness
examples.description: A readiness check asks whether a container should receive traffic. A liveness check asks whether Kubernetes should restart it.
examples.code:
Readiness fails -> stop sending Service traffic to that Pod
Liveness fails repeatedly -> container may restart

examples.title: Read logs and rollout state
examples.description: Logs show the program's messages. Rollout status reports progress while a Deployment changes its Pods.
examples.code:
kubectl logs deployment/club-web
kubectl rollout status deployment/club-web

examples.title: Namespaces organise a cluster
examples.description: A namespace groups namespaced resources. It helps separate teams or practice work, but is not by itself a complete security boundary.
examples.code:
Namespace: club-practice
Deployment: club-web inside club-practice
Service: club-web inside club-practice
